caseStudy.problem: An agency managing several clients on Meta Ads spends hours every week copying figures into Excel, account by account, to produce its reports. And the real problems show up too late: a budget running away, a blocked account, conversions that stop.
caseStudy.solution: Meta Ads Report Studio connects the agency's ad accounts, groups them by client and shows on one screen who is spending, how well, and who needs attention.

features.title: Agency overview
features.text: Every client on one screen: spend and its change, daily trend, conversions, cost per conversion. Clients that need attention come first.

features.title: Alerts that matter
features.text: Spend up 40% or more, cost per conversion up 30% or more, a week with no conversions, an account blocked by payment or review.

features.title: Client page
features.text: KPIs, ratios (CTR, CPC, CPM, CPA), the trend, and a campaign table showing each campaign's real status.

features.title: One-click PDF report
features.text: A one-page A4 report under the agency's name, rebuilt on the server from source data, never from figures the browser sends.

caseStudy.architecture: Next.js 16 (App Router, Server Components, Server Actions), PostgreSQL on Neon with Prisma, Meta Marketing API v21. Amounts are held as integer cents and the browser receives 180 days of rows once: switching between 7, 30 and 90 days is instant, and every period has a previous one to compare against.
security: Least privilege: only public_profile and ads_read are requested. The app can neither edit a campaign nor spend money.
Tokens encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM, sent in an Authorization header and never in a URL.
Every identifier coming from the browser is checked against the signed-in user's own data.
No statistics stored: figures are fetched on demand and cached in memory for ten minutes at most.
Rate limiting on the PDF endpoint and bounded concurrency to stay within Meta's API quota.
caseStudy.quality: Every pull request runs lint, type-check, the Vitest and Testing Library suite, then a production build. The Docker image is then built, started and probed over HTTP.
caseStudy.ctaText: A fictitious agency with six clients, no account or setup needed.
